title: Custom ISAM BTree Database & Network Persistence

contributors.contribution: Provided architecture and implementation consultation during development of the custom database.
The original Version 1 designer, later working part-time, provided domain and architectural consultation.

description: I designed and implemented a custom ISAM BTree database used across the SE through Hydra-Gen generation of the Essential Skills suite, ultimately supporting 60+ production programs. The system could run locally on a workstation or from a shared school file server, allowing teachers and students to work concurrently without requiring a dedicated database server. I built the BTree storage engine, binary record format, indexing, partitioning, locking, retry and recovery architecture, and later integrated the persistence model into Hydra-Gen's broader multi-backend database framework.

sections.title: Production Database for 60+ Programs
paragraphs: The custom ISAM database became part of the core persistence architecture used throughout the SE to Hydra-Gen product lineage rather than remaining an isolated database experiment.
It ultimately supported more than 60 Essential Skills production programs.

sections.title: Built for Real School Infrastructure
paragraphs: Many schools had shared file servers but did not have dedicated SQL or application servers available for educational software.
The persistence layer was therefore designed to work using infrastructure schools already had, with both local-workstation and shared-file-server deployment modes.

sections.title: Local Workstation Mode
paragraphs: Schools could keep persistence entirely on an individual workstation for simple deployment and fast access.

sections.title: Shared Network File-Server Mode
paragraphs: The network version placed the persistence files on a shared school file server.
Teachers could modify students, assignments and reports while students were simultaneously using the learning programs.

sections.title: Filesystem Partitioning
paragraphs: Rather than forcing every user through one monolithic shared database, I partitioned persistence through the filesystem to reduce contention.
Student and teacher data could be separated into individual database areas while only genuinely shared information required coordinated write locking.

sections.title: Custom BTree Storage Engine
paragraphs: I implemented the BTree storage engine myself rather than wrapping an existing database library.
The recovered source confirms a disk-backed BTree with binary records and indexes.

sections.title: Binary Record Storage
paragraphs: Logical tables used binary record and index files rather than serialized Java object graphs.
items: Record relocation when updated data no longer fit in place

sections.title: On-Disk File Structure
paragraphs: The recovered implementation stores table data and indexes in separate files and reserves metadata space for index definitions.
items: Reserved record-file header space for index definitions

sections.title: Composite & Partial-Key Indexing
paragraphs: Indexes could be built from multiple ordered key parts rather than only single primitive keys.
The engine also supported partial-key matching, which allowed application-specific lookup patterns without scanning the entire record set.

sections.title: Record Update & Relocation
paragraphs: When an updated record still fit in its existing space it could be rewritten in place.
When it grew beyond the available space, the engine could append the replacement record and leave relocation information behind.

sections.title: Concurrency & File Locking
paragraphs: The network generation used native/JNI support and filesystem locking behavior to coordinate writes across workstations.
Filesystem permissions and lock files were used as part of the locking strategy.

sections.title: Retry & Timeout Strategy
paragraphs: When another workstation held a required lock, the application retried the operation approximately every half second.
If the lock could not be obtained after roughly 30 seconds, the operation failed with an error rather than hanging indefinitely.

sections.title: Stale-Lock Recovery
paragraphs: Network failures or abnormal shutdowns could occasionally leave stale locking state.
Teachers or administrators had access to a recovery utility that could flush/reset the lock state and allow normal operation to continue.

sections.title: Different Historical Generations
paragraphs: A recovered SmartDB-era copy contains a Java RandomAccessFile version of the ISAM engine where older native locking hooks remain but are disabled.
This appears to represent a different generation or deployment configuration from the earlier network-file-server implementation that used JNI/native locking.

sections.title: Hydra-Gen Multi-Backend Evolution
paragraphs: The custom ISAM engine later became one backend within Hydra-Gen's broader SmartDB/Rosetta persistence architecture.
The same application-level persistence concepts were extended to additional database implementations so deployments were not permanently tied to the original ISAM storage engine.

sections.title: Later Database Options
paragraphs: Later Hydra-Gen work included additional supported persistence plugins such as Berkeley DB and SQL Server.
These were supported alternatives within the evolving database architecture, although I do not remember whether any schools actually deployed those particular backends in production.

historicalNotes: The legacy portfolio card described the ISAM BTree as being used by only a few projects, but Jamie later clarified that it became part of the SE through Hydra-Gen persistence architecture and supported 60+ production programs.
Jamie wrote the custom BTree implementation himself with consultation from the former Sun Microsystems manager/consultant and the original Version 1 product designer.
The original network generation supported both local-workstation and shared-school-file-server deployment.
Jamie remembers JNI/native calls being used for cross-platform concurrency and locking in the network version.
Filesystem permissions and lock files were used for locking.
Locked write attempts retried approximately every 500 milliseconds and timed out after approximately 30 seconds.
A teacher/admin utility could reset stale locking state.
Student and teacher persistence was partitioned through the filesystem to reduce contention.
Shared marks/reporting information required coordinated locking.
Some schools could keep marks/stars locally for faster access, with the tradeoff that students needed to return to the same workstation.

Recovered SmartDB-era source contains a different or later Java-only ISAM implementation where native locking hooks exist historically but active native file I/O/locking is disabled in favor of RandomAccessFile.
This recovered SmartDB snapshot therefore should not be treated as proof that the earlier JNI/network-locking generation never existed.

Recovered source confirms a disk-backed BTree implementation with recursive insertion, node splitting, median promotion, root creation, composite indexes, partial-key matching, variable-length records, logical deletion, record relocation, index checking and rebuild facilities.
Recovered table storage uses .rec, .ind and .lck files.
Recovered BTree nodes are fixed at approximately 512 bytes.
Later Hydra-Gen work supported Berkeley DB and SQL Server as additional database plugins based on Jamie's direct recollection of implementing them.
Berkeley DB and SQL Server should be presented as supported backends, not necessarily as broadly deployed school configurations.
Jamie does not remember whether any schools actually selected Berkeley DB or SQL Server for production deployments.
The exact Berkeley DB API/integration generation is not present in the recovered SmartDB snapshot and should be documented if later source is recovered.
